names-view.date.claimed.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section): the first of its dates, under its name: when it was registered (its claim's time). {{when}} is that date.

names-view.date.renew.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section): the second of its dates: from when this web app renews it (the first time it's open on or after that date). {{when}} is that date.

names-view.date.renew.title.message: This web app renews the domain the first time it's open on or after this date.
names-view.date.renew.title.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section): the tooltip of its date of the next renewal (names-view.date.renew).

names-view.date.until.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section): the last of its dates: until when members can look it up unless it is renewed. {{when}} is that date.

names-view.ended.lapsed.message: It wasn't renewed for 30 days and the week that followed. You can register it again if nobody else has.
names-view.ended.lapsed.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), for a domain that lapsed: the sentence under its state (the card has nothing to edit).

names-view.ended.released.message: You let this domain go. Anyone can register it once the release is public, which takes about 2 hours.
names-view.ended.released.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), for a domain let go: the sentence under its state (the card has nothing to edit).

names-view.ended.lost.message: Another member registered this domain before you, or registered it while yours had lapsed. This web app no longer renews it.
names-view.ended.lost.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), for a domain lost to another owner: the sentence under its state (the card has nothing to edit).

names-view.upkeep_one.message: Reopen this web app by about {{when, date}} to keep this domain.
names-view.upkeep_one.note: The line over the domains' cards in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), when one domain is held: by when this web app must be opened again to renew it. {{when}} is that date.

names-view.upkeep_other.message: Reopen this web app by about {{when, date}} to keep these domains.
names-view.upkeep_other.note: The line over the domains' cards in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), when several are held: by when this web app must be opened again to keep them all (the earliest date any of them works until). {{when}} is that date, {{count}} how many domains.

names-view.upkeep.soon_one.message: <name>{{names}}</name> needs renewing. Leave this web app open for a few hours to keep it.
names-view.upkeep.soon_one.note: The line over the domains' cards in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), in the warning tone, when a domain is in its last week or not renewed in time (its grace). {{names}} is the domain.

names-view.upkeep.soon_other.message: <name>{{names}}</name> need renewing. Leave this web app open for a few hours to keep them.
names-view.upkeep.soon_other.note: The line over the domains' cards in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), in the warning tone, when several domains are in their last week or their grace. {{names}} are the domains, {{count}} how many.

names-view.link.held_one.note: A room connection's link to its Domains pane (the toolbar's Network menu, a machine's Network tab, Connections' cards), when it holds one domain (live, or lost: the pane shows it). {{count}} is 1.

names-view.link.held_other.note: A room connection's link to its Domains pane (the toolbar's Network menu, a machine's Network tab, Connections' cards), when it holds several domains. {{count}} is how many.

names-view.link.attention_one.note: A room connection's link to its Domains pane, in the warning tone, when one of its domains is in its last week, not renewed in time, or lost. {{held}} is the message names-view.link.held (how many it holds), {{count}} is 1.

names-view.link.attention_other.note: A room connection's link to its Domains pane, in the warning tone, when several of its domains are in their last week, not renewed in time, or lost. {{held}} is the message names-view.link.held (how many it holds), {{count}} how many need attention.

names-view.line.serving_one.message: This web app serves the room's domains for this connection: it keeps the records of 1 domain, and synced with {{servers}} other servers lately.
names-view.line.serving_one.note: A room connection's Details and its Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections), while it is connected in this tab: the registry's line on a machine that holds a name. {{count}} is the names it holds, {{servers}} the servers it synced with lately.

names-view.line.serving_other.message: This web app serves the room's domains for this connection: it keeps the records of {{count}} domains, and synced with {{servers}} other servers lately.
names-view.line.serving_other.note: A room connection's Details and its Domains pane on the Home page, while it is connected in this tab: the registry's line on a machine that holds a name. {{count}} is how many names it holds, {{servers}} the servers it synced with lately.

names-view.line.member_one.note: A room connection's Details and its Domains pane on the Home page, while it is connected in this tab: the registry's line on a machine that holds no name: {{count}} the registered names it resolved and keeps, {{servers}} the servers of the room's names it holds now.

names-view.line.member_other.note: A room connection's Details and its Domains pane on the Home page, while it is connected in this tab: the registry's line on a machine that holds no name: {{count}} the registered names it resolved and keeps, {{servers}} the servers of the room's names it holds now.

names-view.machine.new.note: The Home page, a machine's Network tab, an adapter's line of names (machines:AdapterCard.adapter.names): a name whose claim isn't public yet. {{name}} is the name.

names-view.machine.until.note: The Home page, a machine's Network tab, an adapter's line of names (machines:AdapterCard.adapter.names): a name with the date it stops resolving unless this web app renews it. {{name}} is the name, {{when}} that date.

DomainCard.label.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), a registered domain's points: the accessible name of the field holding a subdomain (`git` in git.<name>).

DomainCard.target.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), a registered name's points: the accessible name of the field holding the member's name in the room (or its key) the name or its label points at.

DomainCard.note.message: Each points at a member's name in the room, which can be this connection's or another's. Paste a member's name to point there. A subdomain adds a domain under <name>{{name}}</name>.
DomainCard.note.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), under its points; {{name}} is the domain.

DomainCard.addLabel.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), a registered name: adds a row for a subdomain, pointing at this connection.

DomainCard.removeLabel.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), a registered name: the tooltip and accessible name of the icon that removes a subdomain's row (Save keeps it).

DomainCard.pointHere.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), a registered name: sets every row's target to this connection's name in the room (Save keeps it).

DomainCard.save.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), a registered name: saves where it and its labels point (a new zone, published to the room).

DomainCard.release.note: A domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), a registered name: the button that releases it (after asking), and the confirm button of that question (drawn as a warning).

DomainCard.release.confirm.message: Let <name>{{name}}</name> go? It will stop working for the room's members, and anyone can register it once the release is public.
DomainCard.release.confirm.note: The question asked by a domain card's Let it go (a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section)); {{name}} is the domain.

names-view.badLabel.message: “{{label}}” isn't a subdomain: use letters, digits and inner hyphens, 63 at most, and not two hyphens as its third and fourth characters.
names-view.badLabel.note: Error shown on a domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section) when Save finds a subdomain that isn't a DNS label, or has “--” in its third and fourth places (the punycode prefix's, as in “xn--”); {{label}} is what was typed.

names-view.labelTwice.message: “{{label}}” is listed twice: a subdomain points at one place.
names-view.labelTwice.note: Error shown on a domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section) when Save finds the same subdomain in two rows; {{label}} is the subdomain.

names-view.badTarget.message: “{{target}}” isn't a member's name in the room or a key.
names-view.badTarget.note: Error shown on a domain's card in a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section) when Save finds a target that isn't a member's name (<key>.<room name or tag>.p2p.internal) or a 64-digit key; {{target}} is what was typed.

names.ephemeral.message: A connection that isn't kept in this browser can't hold a domain
names.ephemeral.note: Error in the message bar if a domain is registered on a connection whose key goes with the page (its Domains pane says so instead of offering Register: DomainsPane.ephemeral).

names.registerFailed.note: Error headline in the message bar when registering a name failed (its cause under it); {{name}} is the name.

names.lastWeek_one.message: The domain <name>{{names}}</name> is kept only until about {{when, date}}. Leave this web app open for a few hours, or reopen it before then, to keep it.
names.lastWeek_one.note: Notice in the message bar at load when a registered name is in its last week (it will stop resolving unless renewed and its renewal made public). {{names}} is the name, {{when}} when it stops.

names.lastWeek_other.message: The domains <name>{{names}}</name> are kept only until about {{when, date}}. Leave this web app open for a few hours, or reopen it before then, to keep them.
names.lastWeek_other.note: Notice in the message bar at load when registered names are in their last week. {{names}} are the names, {{count}} how many, {{when}} when the first stops.

connections.demoNetwork.note: The default name of a new connection to the demo network (the project's public server that lets the guest reach a few allowed hosts, such as Alpine's package mirror), as the Network wizard, the Network menu and the Home page's Connections show it. It is stored with the connection, which the user can rename.

NetPickStep.kind.demo.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), its first step: the kind of a connection to the demo network, under the connection's name.

NetKindStep.kind.pickDemo.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the step that asks which kind of connection to make: the name of the choice of the demo network (the project's public server).

NetKindStep.kind.pickDemo.note.message: The project's server gives the machine a small network that reaches only a few allowed hosts, such as Alpine's package mirror, with a daily allowance. Nothing to install, no account.
NetKindStep.kind.pickDemo.note.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the step that asks which kind of connection to make: the line under “The demo network”.

NetWizard.title.demo.message: New connection to the demo network
NetWizard.title.demo.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections): its title on the step that makes a connection to the demo network.

NetDemoStep.demo.note.message: The guest's traffic goes through the project's server, which reaches only the hosts it allows (for now Alpine's package mirror, so apk works) and refuses everything else. Each running machine gets a network of its own; other visitors' machines can't reach it.
NetDemoStep.demo.note.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the demo network's step: its first text, what the connection is.

NetDemoStep.demo.limits.message: Each address has a daily allowance of traffic, and a few machines at once. The page says when the allowance runs low and when it resets.
NetDemoStep.demo.limits.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the demo network's step: its second text, the server's limits.

NetDemoStep.demo.advanced.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the demo network's step: the folded section with the server's address (for a server of one's own).

NetDemoStep.demo.server.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the demo network's step, under “Another server”: the label of the field with the server's address (a wss:// URL; empty: the project's). Also in a connection's Settings on the Home page (its page under Connections).

NetDemoStep.demo.server.note.message: Leave it empty for the project's server. Another must be a wss:// URL; only a server on your computer may use ws://.
NetDemoStep.demo.server.note.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the demo network's step, under “Another server”: the note under the server's field. Also in a connection's Settings on the Home page (its page under Connections).

ConnectionDetails.demo.note.message: The guest's traffic goes through the demo network's server, which reaches only the hosts it allows. The machine's network is its own: it closes when the guest is idle for a while and opens again when the guest sends something.
ConnectionDetails.demo.note.note: A connection's Details on the Home page (its page under Connections, also opened by “Details…” in the toolbar's Network menu), for a connection to the demo network: its first text.

ConnectionDetails.demo.server.note: A connection's Details on the Home page, for a connection to the demo network: the label of the server's address (a wss:// URL), with a Copy button.

ConnectionDetails.demo.status.note: A connection's Details on the Home page, for a connection to the demo network: the label of a command to copy (curl and the gateway's /status URL) that shows the network's numbers inside the guest.

ConnectionDetails.demo.status.note.message: It prints the allowance used today, when it resets, and the destinations refused, so a script in the guest can tell why a download stopped.
ConnectionDetails.demo.status.note.note: A connection's Details on the Home page, for a connection to the demo network: the note under the command that shows the network's numbers inside the guest.

demo-net.notURL.message: “{{input}}” isn't a URL. Enter one such as wss://demonet.example.org/.
demo-net.notURL.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the demo network's step: the error when the server field isn't a URL. {{input}} is what was typed.

demo-net.notWss.message: The demo network's server must be a wss:// URL. Only a server on your computer may use ws://.
demo-net.notWss.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), the demo network's step: the error when the server's URL isn't wss (or ws on your computer).

demo-net.versions.message: The demo network's server speaks another version of the protocol. Reload the page to get the current version of this web app.
demo-net.versions.note: The cause under “Couldn't connect” (the Network menu's status for an adapter on the demo network): the server refused this page's protocol version (close code 4001).

demo-net.origin.message: The demo network's server doesn't accept this site.
demo-net.origin.note: The cause under “Couldn't connect” (the Network menu's status for an adapter on the demo network): the server refused the page's origin (close code 4003), as it does for a copy of the web app hosted elsewhere.

demo-net.protocol.message: This web app and the demo network's server disagreed (close code {{code}}).
demo-net.protocol.note: The cause under “Couldn't connect” (the Network menu's status for an adapter on the demo network): the server closed the connection over a message it couldn't take (a bug of this web app's). {{code}} is the WebSocket close code (1002 or 1009).

demo-net.notFrames.message: The demo network's server sent a malformed message.
demo-net.notFrames.note: The cause under “Couldn't connect” (the Network menu's status for an adapter on the demo network): the server sent something that isn't its framing (this web app closed the connection).

demo-net.unreached.message: This browser refused the demo network's address.
demo-net.unreached.note: The cause under “Couldn't connect” (the Network menu's status for an adapter on the demo network): the browser refused to open the WebSocket at all (a URL it blocks).

demo-net-worker.closed.message: The demo network's server closed the connection.
demo-net-worker.closed.note: The cause under “Couldn't connect” (the Network menu's status for an adapter on the demo network): the connection ended for good for another reason.

demo-net.noExitNodes.message: A connection to the demo network has no exit nodes to choose from.
demo-net.noExitNodes.note: The cause under “Couldn't use that exit node” (Network menu) on a demo network's connection. A detail line.

demo-view.connecting.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): opening the connection to the demo network's server.

demo-view.reconnecting.message: Connecting to the demo network again…
demo-view.reconnecting.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): opening a new connection after the last one ended (the guest gets a new network from the server).

demo-view.connected.address.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): connected, the guest has its address from the server. {{address}} is the guest's IPv4 address.

demo-view.connected.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): connected, before the server's DHCP gave the guest an address.

demo-view.idle.message: The demo network is idle. It connects again when the guest sends something.
demo-view.idle.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server closed the guest's network after a while without traffic; the next packet from the guest opens a new one.

demo-view.spent.message: Connected, but today's allowance is used up: nothing leaves the guest until {{when}}.
demo-view.spent.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent; the guest's network stays but reaches nothing. {{when}} is when the allowance resets (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.spent.noTime.message: Connected, but today's allowance is used up: nothing leaves the guest until it resets.
demo-view.spent.noTime.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent (the server didn't say when it resets).

demo-view.slow.message: Connected, slowly: today's allowance is used up, so everything goes through the slow lane until {{when}}.
demo-view.slow.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent, and the server's slow lane is on: the guest still reaches hosts, but slowly (the allowed hosts too). {{when}} is when the allowance resets (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.slow.noTime.message: Connected, slowly: today's allowance is used up, so everything goes through the slow lane until it resets.
demo-view.slow.noTime.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent, and the server's slow lane is on: the guest still reaches hosts, but slowly (the server didn't say when it resets).

demo-view.wait.unreachable.message: Couldn't reach the demo network's server. Trying again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.unreachable.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the connection never opened (the server is down, or no internet here). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again (sooner at first, then less often).

demo-view.wait.lost.message: Lost the connection to the demo network. Trying again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.lost.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the connection closed without the server saying why (the server or the way to it went down). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again.

demo-view.wait.guests.message: This address already has as many machines on the demo network as the server allows (in this browser or others behind it). Trying again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.guests.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server refused another network for this visitor's address (close code 4008). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again.

demo-view.wait.site.message: The network this browser is on (with the addresses around it) already has as many machines on the demo network as the server allows. Trying again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.site.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server refused another network for this address's site, e.g. a campus or carrier network sharing addresses (close code 4008, site). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again.

demo-view.wait.connections.message: Connected to the demo network too often in the last minute. Trying again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.connections.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server refused this address's connections for a while (close code 4008, connections). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again.

demo-view.wait.full.message: The demo network's server is full. Trying again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.full.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server has as many networks as it takes (close code 4009). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again.

demo-view.wait.bytes.message: Today's allowance on the demo network is used up. It resets at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.bytes.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server refused the connection because this address's daily traffic allowance is spent (close code 4010). {{when}} is when it resets (the page connects again then).

demo-view.wait.bytes.slow.message: Today's allowances on the demo network, the slow lane's too, are used up. They reset at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.bytes.slow.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server refused the connection because this address's daily traffic allowance and its slow lane's allowance are both spent (close code 4010). {{when}} is when they reset (the page connects again then).

demo-view.wait.maintenance.message: The demo network's server is restarting for maintenance. Trying again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.maintenance.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server stopped for a restart (close code 4011). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again (when the server said it would be back).

demo-view.wait.session.message: The demo network's session ended after several hours. Connecting again at {{when}}.
demo-view.wait.session.note: In the Network menu's status line for an adapter on the demo network (also the Home page's Network tab and the status bar's network item): the server ends a network after some hours, so long sessions go through its limits again (close code 4013). {{when}} is the date and time it tries again.

demo-view.budget.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the traffic this address used today, of its daily allowance.

demo-view.budget.resets.message: {{used, bytes}} of today's {{limit, bytes}} used (resets at {{when}})
demo-view.budget.resets.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the traffic this address used today, of its daily allowance. {{when}} is when the count starts again (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.budget.slow.message: {{used, bytes}} of today's {{limit, bytes}} used on the slow lane
demo-view.budget.slow.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the traffic this address used today on the server's slow lane (the hosts off the allowed list, reached slowly), of the slow lane's own daily allowance. Shown only while the server's slow lane is on.

demo-view.slowLane_one.message: Hosts off the allowed list are reached slowly: {{rate, bytes}}/s, {{count}} connection at a time, on ports {{ports}}
demo-view.slowLane_one.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's slow lane is on: hosts not on the allowed list can still be reached, slowly. {{rate}} is this address's speed there (bytes a second), {{count}} how many such connections it may have open at once, {{ports}} the TCP ports the slow lane reaches (numbers, a list).

demo-view.slowLane_other.message: Hosts off the allowed list are reached slowly: {{rate, bytes}}/s, {{count}} connections at a time, on ports {{ports}}
demo-view.slowLane_other.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's slow lane is on: hosts not on the allowed list can still be reached, slowly. {{rate}} is this address's speed there (bytes a second), {{count}} how many such connections it may have open at once, {{ports}} the TCP ports the slow lane reaches (numbers, a list).

demo-view.slowLane.anyPort_one.message: Hosts off the allowed list are reached slowly: {{rate, bytes}}/s, {{count}} connection at a time
demo-view.slowLane.anyPort_one.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's slow lane is on: hosts not on the allowed list can still be reached, slowly. {{rate}} is this address's speed there (bytes a second), {{count}} how many such connections it may have open at once.

demo-view.slowLane.anyPort_other.message: Hosts off the allowed list are reached slowly: {{rate, bytes}}/s, {{count}} connections at a time
demo-view.slowLane.anyPort_other.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's slow lane is on: hosts not on the allowed list can still be reached, slowly. {{rate}} is this address's speed there (bytes a second), {{count}} how many such connections it may have open at once.

demo-view.refused_one.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): how many connections or lookups the server refused (most because their destination isn't on its allowed list). {{names}} is the last few refused, newest first: host names or addresses, with a port where there is one, each with why in parentheses (the demo-view.reason messages).

demo-view.refused_other.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): how many connections or lookups the server refused (most because their destination isn't on its allowed list). {{names}} is the last few refused, newest first: host names or addresses, with a port where there is one, each with why in parentheses (the demo-view.reason messages).

demo-view.refusal.note: One destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): {{what}} is the host name or address, with a port where there is one; {{why}} is the reason, a few words (the demo-view.reason messages).

demo-view.reason.notListed.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): a name or address not on the server's allowed list.

demo-view.reason.port.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): an allowed host, but on a port the server doesn't allow for it (or that no lane reaches).

demo-view.reason.private.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): an address in a private or local range, which the server never reaches.

demo-view.reason.address.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): a connection to an IP address typed directly rather than looked up by name through the server.

demo-view.reason.noName.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): a connection whose first bytes don't say which host it's for (no TLS server name, no HTTP Host).

demo-view.reason.name.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): a connection to an allowed address whose first bytes name another host (another site on the same CDN).

demo-view.reason.egress.message: the server's way out is down
demo-view.reason.egress.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server couldn't reach the internet for it; not the guest's doing.

demo-view.reason.busy.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the guest had too many connections or lookups going at once.

demo-view.reason.udp.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): UDP traffic past the server's DNS, which it doesn't carry.

demo-view.reason.quic.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): HTTP/3 (QUIC, over UDP), which the server doesn't carry; programs fall back to TCP.

demo-view.reason.spent.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): today's traffic allowance is spent.

demo-view.reason.slowConnections.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's slow lane would take it, but this address already has as many slow-lane connections open as it allows.

demo-view.reason.slowSpent.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's slow lane would take it, but the slow lane's daily allowance is spent.

demo-view.reason.unresolved.note: A refusal's reason, in parentheses after the destination in the line under the demo network's status that lists the last destinations the server refused (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): an allowed name that has no address (it doesn't exist, or has no IPv4 address).

demo-view.restart.message: The server restarts for maintenance at {{at}}.
demo-view.restart.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's owner announced a restart. {{at}} is when it goes down.

demo-view.restart.back.message: The server restarts for maintenance at {{at}}, back by {{back}}.
demo-view.restart.back.note: A line under the status line of an adapter on the demo network (the toolbar's Network menu, the Home page's Network tab): the server's owner announced a restart. {{at}} is when it goes down, {{back}} when it's expected back.

demo-view.notice.budget.message: The demo network: this address has used {{percent}}% of today's allowance ({{used, bytes}} of {{limit, bytes}}).
demo-view.notice.budget.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily traffic passed a threshold. {{percent}} is the threshold (80).

demo-view.notice.budget.resets.message: The demo network: this address has used {{percent}}% of today's allowance ({{used, bytes}} of {{limit, bytes}}). It resets at {{when}}.
demo-view.notice.budget.resets.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily traffic passed a threshold. {{percent}} is the threshold (80); {{when}} is when the count starts again (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.notice.spent.message: Today's allowance on the demo network is used up: the guest reaches nothing through it until {{when}}.
demo-view.notice.spent.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent. {{when}} is when it resets (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.notice.spent.noTime.message: Today's allowance on the demo network is used up: the guest reaches nothing through it until it resets.
demo-view.notice.spent.noTime.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent (the server didn't say when it resets).

demo-view.notice.slowed.message: Today's allowance on the demo network is used up: the guest's traffic goes on through the slow lane, slowly, until {{when}}.
demo-view.notice.slowed.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent and the server's slow lane is on, so everything still works, slowly. {{when}} is when it resets (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.notice.slowed.noTime.message: Today's allowance on the demo network is used up: the guest's traffic goes on through the slow lane, slowly, until it resets.
demo-view.notice.slowed.noTime.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily traffic allowance is spent and the server's slow lane is on, so everything still works, slowly (the server didn't say when it resets).

demo-view.notice.slowBudget.message: The demo network: this address has used {{percent}}% of today's slow-lane allowance ({{used, bytes}} of {{limit, bytes}}).
demo-view.notice.slowBudget.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's traffic on the server's slow lane (hosts off the allowed list, reached slowly) passed a threshold of its own daily allowance. {{percent}} is the threshold (80).

demo-view.notice.slowBudget.resets.message: The demo network: this address has used {{percent}}% of today's slow-lane allowance ({{used, bytes}} of {{limit, bytes}}). It resets at {{when}}.
demo-view.notice.slowBudget.resets.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's traffic on the server's slow lane (hosts off the allowed list, reached slowly) passed a threshold of its own daily allowance. {{percent}} is the threshold (80); {{when}} is when the count starts again (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.notice.slowSpent.message: Today's slow-lane allowance on the demo network is used up: until {{when}} the guest reaches only the allowed hosts.
demo-view.notice.slowSpent.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily allowance on the server's slow lane is spent; the allowed hosts still work at full speed. {{when}} is when it resets (the next UTC midnight).

demo-view.notice.slowSpent.noTime.message: Today's slow-lane allowance on the demo network is used up: until it resets the guest reaches only the allowed hosts.
demo-view.notice.slowSpent.noTime.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the address's daily allowance on the server's slow lane is spent; the allowed hosts still work at full speed (the server didn't say when it resets).

demo-view.notice.back.message: The demo network's allowance has reset: the guest reaches the allowed hosts again.
demo-view.notice.back.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): a new day (or a larger allowance) after it was spent.

demo-view.notice.restart.message: The demo network's server restarts for maintenance at {{at}}.
demo-view.notice.restart.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the server's owner announced a restart. {{at}} is when it goes down.

demo-view.notice.restart.back.message: The demo network's server restarts for maintenance at {{at}}, and should be back by {{back}}.
demo-view.notice.restart.back.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): the server's owner announced a restart. {{at}} is when it goes down, {{back}} when it's expected back.

demo-view.notice.lost.message: Lost the connection to the demo network. Trying again…
demo-view.notice.lost.note: The message bar, while a machine runs with an adapter on the demo network (waarm64-demonet, the project's public server): a connected adapter's connection closed without the server saying why; the page tries again by itself.

NetWizard.title.change.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections): its title on its first step when the adapter already has a connection, which asks whether to edit that connection or attach another (NetChangeStep.*).

NetChangeStep.edit.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), its first step on an adapter that already has a connection (title network.NetWizard.title.change): the first choice, which closes the wizard and opens that connection's Settings on the Home page. {{name}} is the connection's name.

NetChangeStep.edit.note.message: Change the settings of the connection attached to this adapter. This opens the connection's page.
NetChangeStep.edit.note.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), its first step on an adapter that already has a connection: the line under network.NetChangeStep.edit.

NetChangeStep.other.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), its first step on an adapter that already has a connection: the second choice, which goes on to the wizard's steps (pick a connection, or make one).

NetChangeStep.other.note.message: Choose another connection for this adapter, or create one. <name>{{name}}</name> stays in this browser.
NetChangeStep.other.note.note: The Network wizard (a dialog opened from the toolbar's Network menu, or the Home page's Network tab and Connections), its first step on an adapter that already has a connection: the line under network.NetChangeStep.other. {{name}} is the name of the connection attached now.

ConnectionTailcatSettings.address.note: A tailcat connection's Settings on the Home page (its page under Connections), under “Go online through a computer” (network.NetTailcatStep.tailcat.exit): the label of the field (hidden by default, with a Show icon) holding the address of the tailcat server it goes online through, which starts with “tc”.

DomainsPane.meta.message: Domains that the connection <name>{{name}}</name> holds in the room <name>{{room}}</name>. They end in .{{domain}}, which guests can usually leave out.
DomainsPane.meta.note: The small line beside the title of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section). {{name}} is the connection's name, {{room}} the room's (its ID without a private room's suffix), {{domain}} the room's domain (`<room name>.p2p.internal`, or `<tag>.p2p.internal` when the room's ID isn't a plain DNS label).

DomainsPane.register.note: The button in the head of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), and again under its first explainer while it has no domains; also a room connection's link to that pane while it has none (the toolbar's Network menu, a machine's Network tab, Connections' cards). It opens a dialog to register a domain in the room for this connection (docs/networking/names.md, where it is a "name").

DomainsIntro.title.message: Give this connection a name other people can remember
DomainsIntro.title.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: its first heading.

DomainsIntro.what.message: A domain is a short name of your choice, such as mybox, that the room's members can use to reach this connection. Without one, they need its own name in the room, which is {{member}}. A domain can also have subdomains, and each can point at this connection or at another member.
DomainsIntro.what.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the first paragraph, what a domain is. {{member}} is the connection's own name in the room (`<key>.<room name>.p2p.internal`).

DomainsIntro.free.message: Registering is free and needs no account. No central server keeps the room's domains. The members who hold domains keep the records and answer lookups for everyone else.
DomainsIntro.free.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the second paragraph, what registering costs and who keeps the records.

DomainsIntro.steps.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the heading of its numbered steps.

DomainsIntro.step.choose.message: Choose a domain. A domain belongs to whoever registered it first and has renewed it ever since.
DomainsIntro.step.choose.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: step 1 (its first words stressed).

DomainsIntro.step.wait.message: Wait about 2 hours. Until then the domain is reserved. It already works in machines that use this connection, but other members can't look it up yet. The wait is the time it takes to prove publicly when you registered.
DomainsIntro.step.wait.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: step 2 (its first words stressed): the claim's timestamp.

DomainsIntro.step.reopen.message: Reopen this web app at least every 2 weeks. It renews your domains while it's open, and no machine needs to be running. A domain that goes 30 days without a renewal stops working, and a week after that anyone can register it.
DomainsIntro.step.reopen.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: step 3 (its first words stressed): the renewals.

DomainsIntro.before.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the heading of its list of things to know.

DomainsIntro.before.reach.message: Members who know a domain can reach the connection it points at and see when that connection is online. Nobody can list the room's domains, but any member can check whether a name they guess is registered.
DomainsIntro.before.reach.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the list's first item: who sees what.

DomainsIntro.before.serve.message: While this connection is connected, this web app keeps the room's domain records and helps other members look domains up.
DomainsIntro.before.serve.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the list's second item: the connection serves the room's domains.

DomainsIntro.before.copy.message: This browser holds the only copy of your domains. If its data is cleared, they are lost. To keep a copy, use <ui>Back up key and domains…</ui>.
DomainsIntro.before.copy.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the list's third item: the backup (a command in the connection's left column, machines:ConnectionNav.backup).

DomainsIntro.before.services.message: Domains rely on decentralized infrastructure. To use them, the browsers of the room's members may contact Nostr relays, OpenTimestamps servers, and Bitcoin block explorers. No payment or wallet is involved.
DomainsIntro.before.services.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the list's fourth item: the outside services.

DomainsIntro.before.earlier.message: Rarely, a domain that looked free turns out to have an earlier registration, for example by a member who was away when you registered. The earlier registration wins, and this web app tells you when that happens.
DomainsIntro.before.earlier.note: The first explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), shown in the cards' place while the connection has no domains: the list's last item: a domain lost to an earlier claim.

DomainsHow.summary.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the summary line that unfolds it (collapsed by default).

DomainsHow.keep.title.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: its first heading.

DomainsHow.keep.message: This web app renews each domain about every 2 weeks, while it's open. No machine needs to be running, and a short visit is enough. A domain that goes 30 days without a renewal stops working for the room's members. You can still renew it for a week after that by reopening this web app. Then it lapses, and anyone can register it.
DomainsHow.keep.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the paragraph on renewals.

DomainsHow.states.title.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the heading of its list of states.

DomainsHow.states.preparing.message: Preparing. This web app is doing the work a registration requires, which takes up to a minute or two.
DomainsHow.states.preparing.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the states' list, Preparing (its first word stressed).

DomainsHow.states.reserved.message: Reserved. The domain is registered but not public yet. It already works in machines that use this connection. Other members can look it up about 2 hours after you registered it.
DomainsHow.states.reserved.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the states' list, Reserved.

DomainsHow.states.active.message: Active. Members can look the domain up.
DomainsHow.states.active.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the states' list, Active.

DomainsHow.states.grace.message: Not renewed in time. Members can't look the domain up until this web app renews it.
DomainsHow.states.grace.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the states' list, the week of grace.

DomainsHow.states.ended.message: Lapsed, let go, or lost. The domain is no longer yours.
DomainsHow.states.ended.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the states' list, the three ends.

DomainsHow.who.title.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the heading on who sees what.

DomainsHow.who.message: Members who know a domain can reach the connection it points at and see when that connection is online. Nobody can list the room's domains, but any member can check whether a name they guess is registered. Domains can be looked up only while at least one member that holds a domain is connected to the room.
DomainsHow.who.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the paragraph on who sees what.

DomainsHow.where.title.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the heading on where domains are kept.

DomainsHow.where.message: This browser holds the only copy of your domains. If its data is cleared, they are lost. To keep a copy, or to move them to another browser, use <ui>Back up key and domains…</ui>. Domains rely on decentralized infrastructure. To use them, the browsers of the room's members may contact Nostr relays, OpenTimestamps servers, and Bitcoin block explorers.
DomainsHow.where.note: The second explainer of a room connection's Domains pane on the Home page (its page under Connections, its Domains section), folded under its summary once the connection has domains: the paragraph on the only copy, the backup (machines:ConnectionNav.backup) and the outside services.

ConnectionBackup.title.note: Back up key and domains (a dialog opened from a room connection's left column on the Home page): its title.

ConnectionBackup.intro.message: This is the key of the connection <name>{{name}}</name>, followed by its domains. Copy it and keep it somewhere safe.
ConnectionBackup.intro.note: Back up key and domains (a dialog opened from a room connection's left column on the Home page): the line above the field, when the connection holds domains. {{name}} is the connection's name.

ConnectionBackup.intro.none.message: This is the key of the connection <name>{{name}}</name>. It has no domains yet. Copy it and keep it somewhere safe.
ConnectionBackup.intro.none.note: Back up key and domains (a dialog opened from a room connection's left column on the Home page): the line above the field, when the connection holds no domains. {{name}} is the connection's name.

ConnectionBackup.label.note: Back up key and domains (a dialog opened from a room connection's left column on the Home page): the label of the field holding the export (hidden until shown, with Copy).

ConnectionBackup.warning.message: Keep it secret. Whoever has it can take this connection's name and address in the room, and its domains.
ConnectionBackup.warning.note: Back up key and domains (a dialog opened from a room connection's left column on the Home page): the warning under the field.

ConnectionBackup.restore.message: To restore it, create or join the room in a new connection, open <ui>Advanced</ui>, choose <ui>A key to paste</ui>, and paste it there. Don't connect two connections with the same key at the same time.
ConnectionBackup.restore.note: Back up key and domains (a dialog opened from a room connection's left column on the Home page): how to restore it (the Network wizard's room step: Advanced, its key choice).

ConnectionBackup.close.note: Back up key and domains (a dialog opened from a room connection's left column on the Home page): the button that closes it.
